subproblems.title: The initial velocity of a compact variation is a C¹ test field supported in K
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, U ⊆ E, φ : ℝ → E → E, ε ∈ ℝ and K ⊆ E. Suppose IsCompactVariation φ ε K holds: ε > 0; K is compact; (t, x) ↦ φ t x is C^∞ on (−ε, ε) × E; for |t| < ε, φ t is bijective with C^∞ Function.invFun (φ t); φ 0 = id; and φ t x = x whenever |t| < ε and x ∉ K. Suppose also K ⊆ U. Then the initial velocity X_φ(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0 is a test field in U: X_φ is C¹, has compact support, and tsupport X_φ ⊆ U (in fact tsupport X_φ ⊆ K).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (φ : ℝ → Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (ε : ℝ) (K : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), IsCompactVariation φ ε K → K ⊆ U → IsTestField U (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) (a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, hence complete and Hausdorff). IsCompactVariation φ ε K consists of the fields (pos) 0 < ε; (compact) K is compact; (smooth) (t, x) ↦ φ t x is C^∞ on S := Ioo(−ε, ε) ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ × E; (diffeo) for t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε), φ t is bijective with C^∞ Function.invFun (φ t); (init) φ 0 x = x; (fixed) φ t x = x for t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε) and x ∉ K. IsTestField U Z means: Z is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 Z), Z has compact support, and tsupport Z ⊆ U. Write Φ(q) := φ q.1 q.2 for q ∈ ℝ × E and X_φ(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0. Only the fields pos, compact, smooth and fixed are used, together with the hypothesis K ⊆ U.

1. (The domain.) S is open in ℝ × E, being the product of the open interval Ioo(−ε, ε) and the whole space. By (pos), 0 ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε), so (0, y) ∈ S for every y ∈ E. By (smooth), Φ is C^∞ on S.

2. (Velocity formula.) Fix y ∈ E. Since S is an open neighbourhood of (0, y) and Φ is C^∞ on S, Φ is C^∞ at (0, y). In particular it is differentiable there, with Fréchet derivative DΦ(0, y) : ℝ × E → E. The curve g(t) := (t, y) satisfies g(0) = (0, y) and has derivative (1, 0) at 0. By the chain rule, the function t ↦ φ t y = Φ(g(t)) has derivative DΦ(0, y)(1, 0) at t = 0. Hence X_φ(y) = DΦ(0, y)(1, 0) for every y ∈ E.

3. (Regularity.) Since S is open and Φ is C^∞ on S, the derivative map q ↦ DΦ(q) is C¹ on S: on an open set, a C^N map has a C^m derivative whenever m + 1 ≤ N, and here 1 + 1 ≤ ∞. The affine map y ↦ (0, y) is C^∞ from E to ℝ × E and takes values in S (step 1). So the composite y ↦ DΦ(0, y) is C¹ on all of E. Evaluating a C¹ family of continuous linear maps at the fixed vector (1, 0) gives a C¹ map, because evaluation is a continuous bilinear operation. By step 2, X_φ = (y ↦ DΦ(0, y)(1, 0)). Hence X_φ is C¹.

4. (Vanishing off K.) Let y ∉ K. By (fixed), φ t y = y for every t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε), and this interval is a neighbourhood of 0 by (pos). So t ↦ φ t y agrees with the constant function t ↦ y on a neighbourhood of 0. The derivative at a point depends only on the germ there, so X_φ(y) = deriv (t ↦ y) 0 = 0.

5. (Support.) By step 4, support X_φ ⊆ K. By (compact), K is compact, hence closed in the Hausdorff space E. Therefore tsupport X_φ = closure(support X_φ) ⊆ K. A function vanishing outside a compact set has compact support, since its tsupport is a closed subset of that compact set; so X_φ has compact support. Finally, tsupport X_φ ⊆ K ⊆ U by hypothesis.

6. (Conclusion.) Steps 3 and 5 give ContDiff ℝ 1 X_φ, HasCompactSupport X_φ and tsupport X_φ ⊆ U, i.e. IsTestField U (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0). ∎

subproblems.title: y + t·X(y) is a compact variation with initial velocity X (smooth compactly supported X)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, and let X : E → E be C^∞ with compact support. Then there is ε ∈ ℝ (for instance ε = 1/(L+1) with L = sup‖DX‖) such that φ(t, y) := y + t•X(y) satisfies IsCompactVariation φ ε (tsupport X): ε > 0; tsupport X is compact; φ is C^∞ on (−ε, ε) × E; for |t| < ε, φ_t is bijective with C^∞ Function.invFun φ_t; φ_0 = id; and φ_t(y) = y for y ∉ tsupport X. Moreover the initial velocity is X: deriv (t ↦ y + t•X(y)) 0 = X(y) for every y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (X : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ), ContDiff ℝ ∞ X → HasCompactSupport X → ∃ ε : ℝ, IsCompactVariation (fun t y ↦ y + t • X y) ε (tsupport X) ∧ (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t : ℝ ↦ y + t • X y) 0) = X
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, hence a complete normed space. DX(y) ∈ L(E, E) denotes the Fréchet derivative and I = id_E. Put φ_t(y) := y + t•X(y), so the variation is φ = (fun t y ↦ y + t • X y). IsCompactVariation φ ε K consists of the fields (pos) 0 < ε; (compact) K is compact; (smooth) (t, y) ↦ φ t y is C^∞ on Ioo(−ε, ε) ×ˢ univ; (diffeo) for t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε), φ t is bijective and Function.invFun (φ t) is C^∞; (init) φ 0 y = y; (fixed) φ t y = y for t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε) and y ∉ K. Here K = tsupport X.

1. (Bounds on X.) X is C^∞, hence C¹, so DX is continuous. DX vanishes outside the closed set tsupport X, because X vanishes on a neighbourhood of every point outside it. So DX has compact support. A continuous function with compact support is bounded: there is C with ‖DX(y)‖ ≤ C for all y. Put L := max(C, 0) ≥ 0; then ‖DX(y)‖ ≤ L for all y. By the mean value inequality, X is L-Lipschitz: ‖X(y) − X(y')‖ ≤ L‖y − y'‖ for all y, y'.

2. (Choice of ε; pos and compact.) Put ε := 1/(L + 1) > 0. Field (compact) holds because HasCompactSupport X means precisely that tsupport X is compact.

3. (smooth) The map (t, y) ↦ y + t•X(y) is C^∞ on ℝ × E. It is the sum of the projection (t, y) ↦ y and the product of the smooth scalar function (t, y) ↦ t with the smooth map (t, y) ↦ X(y). In particular it is C^∞ on Ioo(−ε, ε) ×ˢ univ.

4. (init and fixed) φ_0(y) = y + 0•X(y) = y. If y ∉ tsupport X then y ∉ support X, so X(y) = 0 and φ_t(y) = y for every t.

5. (diffeo) Fix t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε). Then |t| < 1/(L + 1), so c := |t|L ≤ L/(L + 1) < 1.
 5a. (Perturbation of the identity.) For all y, y' we have φ_t(y) − φ_t(y') − (y − y') = t•(X(y) − X(y')), hence ‖φ_t(y) − φ_t(y') − (y − y')‖ ≤ |t|L‖y − y'‖ = c‖y − y'‖. Consequently ‖φ_t(y) − φ_t(y')‖ ≥ (1 − c)‖y − y'‖, so φ_t is injective.
 5b. (Surjectivity, homeomorphism.) Let z ∈ E. The map T_z(y) := z − t•X(y) satisfies ‖T_z(y) − T_z(y')‖ ≤ c‖y − y'‖ with c < 1. Since E is complete, the Banach fixed point theorem gives a fixed point y with y = z − t•X(y), i.e. φ_t(y) = z. So φ_t is a continuous bijection of E. By 5a its inverse is (1 − c)^{-1}-Lipschitz, so φ_t is a homeomorphism h of E. (If E = {0}, i.e. n + ℓ = 0, everything is trivial.)
 5c. (Invertible derivative.) φ_t is differentiable at every a ∈ E, with Dφ_t(a) = I + t DX(a), and ‖t DX(a)‖ ≤ |t|L = c < 1. In the Banach algebra L(E, E), 1 − u is invertible whenever ‖u‖ < 1 (Neumann series). Taking u := −t DX(a) shows that I + t DX(a) is invertible, i.e. a continuous linear equivalence of E.
 5d. (Smooth inverse.) h = φ_t is C^∞ (step 3 with t fixed), h is a homeomorphism, and its derivative at every point is a continuous linear equivalence (5c). By the inverse function theorem in the form 'a C^k homeomorphism of a Banach space whose derivative is everywhere invertible has a C^k inverse', h^{-1} is C^∞.
 5e. (Function.invFun.) φ_t is surjective, so for each z, Function.invFun φ_t z is a preimage of z: φ_t(Function.invFun φ_t z) = z. Also φ_t(h^{-1}(z)) = z, and φ_t is injective, so Function.invFun φ_t z = h^{-1}(z). Hence Function.invFun φ_t = h^{-1} is C^∞. Together with 5b this proves (diffeo).

6. (Velocity.) For fixed y, the map t ↦ y + t•X(y) is affine in t, with derivative X(y) at every t: the derivative of t ↦ t•v is v, and adding the constant y does not change it. Hence deriv (fun t : ℝ ↦ y + t•X(y)) 0 = X(y) for every y. By function extensionality, (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t : ℝ ↦ y + t • X y) 0) = X.

Steps 2–6 show that ε = 1/(L + 1) satisfies IsCompactVariation (fun t y ↦ y + t • X y) ε (tsupport X), together with the velocity identity, which proves the statement. ∎

Then there are a compact set K with tsupport X ⊆ K ⊆ U and maps Y_k : E → E (k ∈ ℕ) such that each Y_k is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport Y_k ⊆ K, and DY_k → DX uniformly on E as k → ∞.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) is finite-dimensional, hence proper. volume is Lebesgue measure on E, an additive Haar measure invariant under x ↦ −x. IsTestField U X means: X is C¹, X has compact support, and tsupport X ⊆ U. K_0 := tsupport X is compact and K_0 ⊆ U. For ψ : E → ℝ continuous with compact support and G : E → F continuous (F a real Banach space), (ψ ⋆ G)(x) := ∫ ψ(t) G(x − t) dt. cthickening δ A = {y : infEdist(y, A) ≤ δ}; it equals {y : dist(y, A) ≤ δ} for A ≠ ∅, and ∅ for A = ∅.

1. (The compact set K.) K_0 is compact, U is open and K_0 ⊆ U. So there is δ > 0 with K := cthickening δ K_0 ⊆ U. [Standard argument: otherwise pick y_j ∉ U and x_j ∈ K_0 with dist(y_j, x_j) ≤ 2/j. A subsequence of (x_j) converges to some x ∈ K_0 ⊆ U, and then y_j → x along it, which contradicts the openness of U.] K is closed and bounded in the proper space E, hence compact, and K_0 ⊆ K.

2. (Mollifiers.) For k ∈ ℕ put r_k := δ/(k + 2), so 0 < r_k < δ and r_k → 0. Let ψ_k : E → ℝ be the normalized smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius r_k/2 and outer radius r_k. Then ψ_k is C^∞, ψ_k ≥ 0, ∫ ψ_k = 1, support ψ_k = ball(0, r_k), and ψ_k has compact support. Define Y_k := ψ_k ⋆ X, i.e. Y_k(x) = ∫ ψ_k(t) X(x − t) dt.

3. (Smoothness.) ψ_k is C^∞ with compact support, and X is continuous, hence locally integrable. Writing Y_k(x) = ∫ ψ_k(x − s) X(s) ds and differentiating under the integral sign arbitrarily often (all derivatives of ψ_k are bounded and compactly supported) shows that Y_k is C^∞.

4. (Support.) Suppose Y_k(x) ≠ 0. Then ψ_k(t)X(x − t) ≠ 0 for some t, so x = t + (x − t) with t ∈ ball(0, r_k) and x − t ∈ support X ⊆ K_0. Then dist(x, x − t) = ‖t‖ < r_k < δ, so x ∈ cthickening δ K_0 = K. Thus support Y_k ⊆ K. Since K is closed, tsupport Y_k ⊆ K, and since K is compact, Y_k has compact support.

5. (Derivative of Y_k.) X is C¹ with compact support and ψ_k is locally integrable, so we may differentiate under the integral sign in x. The derivative of x ↦ ψ_k(t)X(x − t) is ψ_k(t)DX(x − t), which for x in a fixed ball is dominated by |ψ_k(t)| sup‖DX‖ times the indicator of a compact set. Hence DY_k(x) = ∫ ψ_k(t) DX(x − t) dt = (ψ_k ⋆ DX)(x) for every x ∈ E.

6. (Uniform convergence.) DX is continuous and vanishes off the compact set K_0, so DX is uniformly continuous on E (Heine–Cantor for compactly supported functions). Let η > 0, and choose ρ > 0 with ‖DX(x') − DX(x)‖ < η/2 whenever ‖x' − x‖ < ρ. Choose N ∈ ℕ with N > δ/ρ; then for k ≥ N, r_k = δ/(k + 2) < δ/N < ρ. Fix such a k and any x ∈ E. If ψ_k(t) ≠ 0 then ‖t‖ < r_k < ρ, so ‖DX(x − t) − DX(x)‖ ≤ η/2. Using ψ_k ≥ 0 and ∫ ψ_k = 1,
 ‖DY_k(x) − DX(x)‖ = ‖∫ ψ_k(t)(DX(x − t) − DX(x)) dt‖ ≤ ∫ ψ_k(t)‖DX(x − t) − DX(x)‖ dt ≤ η/2 < η.
So sup_x ‖DY_k(x) − DX(x)‖ < η for all k ≥ N, i.e. TendstoUniformly (fun k ↦ fderiv ℝ (Y k)) (fderiv ℝ X) atTop.

Steps 1–6 produce K (compact, K ⊆ U, tsupport X ⊆ K) and (Y_k) (each C^∞, compactly supported, tsupport Y_k ⊆ K) with DY_k → DX uniformly, which is the statement. ∎
